name: MGIC Investment Corp
verdict: WATCH (limit-if-it-comes; NMIH is the MI to own instead) — CLEAN but an ex-growth peak-harvester at 1.24x book; ~17-21% of FY25 earnings is fading reserve release and the loss ratio just turned positive. No lying-detector flag; the catch is a valuation/allocation judgment.
entry_band: WATCH — no fresh buy at 1.24x book / top-of-range. If owned at all, GTC BUY $25.75 (~11% below live $28.96, just above the 52/13wk low $24.71 ~= 1.05x book), ~0.5% of the $1M base (~$5k) — liquidity utterly non-binding ($59.5M ADV; clip ~0.01% of ADV). This is a limit-if-it-comes-to-you for a no-growth 14% ROE + big buyback, NOT a chase. But the single MI slot goes to NMIH, so MTG's own order stays a bench line.
kill_triggers: Reserve-release runs out faster than modeled: current-accident-year loss ratio keeps rising (crossed to +5.1% in FY25 from -1.5%) and the prior-year favorable development (now $155M, down from $404M in FY22) goes to ~zero -> the mid-teens ROE normalizes DOWN and 1.24x book is exposed as a peak multiple
Delinquency inventory acceleration (2.43% and rising; new notices up) turning from 'normalizing' into a genuine credit cycle -> loss ratio spike, the standard MI downturn
A housing/credit downturn: MI losses are convex to home-price declines + unemployment; a real HPA reversal is the sector-level tail (shared by NMIH)

Capital return outpacing a shrinking earnings base (returning ~100% now) forces holdco cash down or PMIERs cushion erosion — currently very strong ($2.5B/78%), so this is a distant risk, but the buyback is the only BVPS growth engine

court_record.dd: WATCH 5/10 — CLEAN, well-capitalized, high-quality, but ex-growth peak-harvester; the diligence value is the MI head-to-head that routes the slot to NMIH. MODE B (led): peak-cycle hypothesis CONFIRMED and openly disclosed. (1) Favorable prior-year reserve development funded 37.1%/23.1%/21.9%/16.7% of PRETAX income FY22/23/24/25 (46.7%/29.2%/27.9%/21.0% of NET income); the release is SHRINKING ($404.1M->$208.5M->$212.5M->$155.2M) and the reported loss ratio crossed back above zero (-25.3%/-2.2%/-1.5%/+5.1%) — FY25 is the first year current-AY losses out-ran the release. MGIC's own words: the post-COVID delinquency decline 'resulted in favorable loss reserve development... and increased net income.' ~17-21% of FY25 earnings is still release, not current underwriting -> the mid-teens ROE is flattered and normalizes down. (2) Delinquency inventory 25,650->26,791->27,072 (rate 2.25%->2.40%->2.43%); new notices 51,427->53,006 rising; claims-received inventory 302->319->398 — direction is up, cures past peak. (3) PMIERs Available Assets $5.7B, excess $2.5B over ~$3.2B min (~78% cushion) — capital NOT the risk. (4) Persistency 84.8%, near the top of its range (trough 60.7% Q1-21) = a late-cycle rate-lock tailwind that inflates earned-premium persistence exactly when already highest; 80% of RIF post-2019, 44% post-2022. (5) Capital-return = harvest tell: OpCo upstreamed $800M to holdco FY25; holdco returned ~$915M ($789M buyback + $132M div); shares 320.3M->219.4M (-31%) over 4yr; book-equity CAGR +1.4% (flat), NI CAGR +3.8% (plateaued), BVPS +11.5%/yr ENTIRELY buyback-made. (6) Takeaway-vs-data: NO divergence — release magnitude, rising DQ, roll-forward, 'normalizing to pre-COVID' all printed -> a fully-disclosed peak is CLEAN per honesty-alpha; the catch is valuation/allocation not a lie. (7) Identity reconciles PERFECTLY: implied P/E = 1.234/0.143 = 8.60x = reported (mcap $6.35B / FY25 NI $738M) 8.60x -> book & earnings basis clean. MODE A: CIK 876437; FY25 10-K 2026-02-25, Q1-26 10-Q 2026-04-29. Cap structure CLEAN — no preferred (0 hits), no live converts (9% conv jr sub debentures converted/purchased away), only 5.25% Sr Notes $646M due Aug-2028, LTD/equity 12.6%. Book $5.148B / 219.367M sh -> BVPS $23.47 -> P/B 1.234 at $28.96 (screen 1.24 confirmed to 3 decimals). FY25 NI $738.3M, ROE 14.3% (5yr avg 15.1%).
court_record.adjudication: WATCH — a clean, honestly-disclosed, strongly-capitalized mortgage insurer that is nonetheless a mature capital-return machine harvesting the tail end of a benign credit cycle, priced at 1.24x book near the top of its range with ROE partly funded by a depleting reserve-release. No honesty flag (fully disclosed). The decisive diligence output is the MTG-vs-NMIH head-to-head: at an IDENTICAL ~1.22x P/B / ~8x P/E, NMIH grows book ~+13%/yr organically (vs MTG +1.4%) AND shrinks the count, with a higher/steadier ROE (17.2%/1% vs 15.1%/2%). The single mortgage-insurer slot therefore goes to NMIH; MTG is WATCH-only, a limit-if-it-comes into the low-$25s, and its liquidity/dividend edge is immaterial at a $5-10k clip.

edge_explainer.market_believes: A cheap, well-run, well-capitalized mortgage insurer at ~8.6x earnings / 1.24x book returning ~100% of capital — quality on sale.
edge_explainer.we_believe: Correct that it's clean and well-capitalized, but it's an EX-GROWTH peak-harvester: book has been flat (+1.4%/yr), ~17-21% of FY25 earnings is a FADING reserve release, the loss ratio just turned positive, and BVPS growth is entirely the buyback. At an identical multiple, NMIH is a +13%-organic-growth compounder — same price, better engine.
edge_explainer.why_we_might_have_edge: The diligence contribution is (a) quantifying the reserve-release share of earnings and its decline (the peak-cycle proof), and (b) the MTG-vs-NMIH decomposition that routes the single MI slot to the compounder for the same price — an allocation edge, not a mispricing.
edge_explainer.why_it_might_be_priced_in: At 8.6x / 1.24x with the identity reconciling exactly and everything disclosed, MTG is fairly-to-fully priced for what it is; there's no hidden distortion to exploit — which is precisely why it's WATCH, not a buy.
edge_explainer.what_resolves_it: The release running out (loss ratio normalizing up) is the slow-motion resolver; a housing downturn is the fast one. Neither is a positive catalyst — the name is dead-money-ish at 1.24x absent a pullback.
edge_explainer.mechanism_falsifier: If current-accident-year underwriting margins prove structurally higher than pre-COVID (so the mid-teens ROE is NOT release-flattered), the peak-harvester thesis weakens and 1.24x could be fair-for-growth — but 4yr flat book argues against it.
edge_explainer.edge_type: VALUE (none, net) — a clean but fully-priced peak-harvester; own NMIH instead. MTG is a low-$25s limit-if-it-comes bench line, not a table-pound.
